name: albitor-plugins
description: Albitor's catalogue of Claude Code plugins.

plugins.name: gds
plugins.description: Build and audit GOV.UK-compliant services: GOV.UK Design System components, patterns and styles, plus WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility and the public sector accessibility regulations.

plugins.name: shadcn
plugins.description: Build, audit, and preview modern web apps with shadcn/ui components on Radix UI primitives and Tailwind CSS, meeting WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility. The default design system for net-new SME and startup web apps.

plugins.name: mui
plugins.description: Build, audit, and preview Material Design interfaces in the app's own framework (Svelte SMUI/m3-svelte, React @mui/material): the shared Material system (colour, type, spacing, elevation, theming) and component inventory, plus WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility for consumer and general-purpose web apps.

plugins.name: carbon
plugins.description: Build and audit enterprise, data-heavy B2B interfaces with the IBM Carbon Design System: Carbon components (React and Web Components), patterns, IBM Design Language styles and tokens, plus WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility and an axe-based conformance baseline.

plugins.name: auth
plugins.description: The default auth pack: end-user sign-up and sign-in for a delivered app, backed by an Amazon Cognito user pool. Ships templated files (pool and public client, the API's token check and GET /api/me, the sign-in, sign-up, confirm-code and reset screens) that the platform renders into a new BYOA app's first commit, and a skill for what each build still writes. Self-sign-up is on by default; email verification is required.

plugins.name: docs
plugins.description: Author an app's documentation with three authoritative frameworks: Diátaxis (the four documentation modes), the C4 model (software architecture diagrams), and arc42 (the 12-section architecture template). The first-party required-documentation capability skills.

plugins.name: web-svelte
plugins.description: The web-framework plugin for SvelteKit: a static SPA build, file routing, the shell that hosts providers, the route guard and the nav, error, 404 and offline pages, a small API client, both client data layers (online-only TanStack Query, or offline-first outbox and sync) with the one the platform selects as the entry point, and the web side of the local run contract.

plugins.name: api-go
plugins.description: The api-runtime plugin: a Go HTTP server skeleton with request logging and correlation ids, a middleware chain, routes and paging, a health route, an OpenAPI contract and the local test issuer, behind the api.middleware and api.routes slots.

plugins.name: test-playwright
plugins.description: The test-harness plugin: a Playwright journey harness with a watched browser context, one sign-in for the suite and local test identities, fixtures that clean up after themselves, an axe WCAG 2.2 A/AA audit, and a read-only CI workflow.

plugins.name: deploy-byoa-aws
plugins.description: The deploy-target plugin for a customer's own AWS account: Terraform rendered from albitor.yaml (CloudFront and S3 for the site, API Gateway and a Lambda for the API, DynamoDB tables, alarms, optional DNS) from versioned modules, the CI and deploy workflows, the stale state-lock guard, the preview's demo and verifier accounts, and the owner's invite workflow.

plugins.name: deploy-hosted
plugins.description: The deploy-target plugin for the hosted lane: no infrastructure in the repository, the platform compiles albitor.yaml and deploys it. Ships the managed CI workflow that checks the manifest and builds and tests the API and the web app.

plugins.name: data-dynamodb
plugins.description: The data-store plugin: a Store interface for the Go API over one DynamoDB table (string pk and sk, revisions, cursor paging), the in-memory fake for local runs and tests, the data-store@1 conformance suite, and the services.tables fragment. No Terraform: the deploy target realises the table.

plugins.name: kit-shadcn
plugins.description: The component-kit plugin for Svelte: the styled shell pieces (app shell, nav, forms, tables, dialogs, toasts, empty states) in the shadcn style on Bits UI, themed by one set of colour tokens that pass WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in light and dark.

plugins.name: auth-cognito
plugins.description: The auth plugin for the default profile: Amazon Cognito sign-up and sign-in. The API verifies tokens and serves GET /api/me and the sign-in calls (managed, standard library only), the web side keeps a provider-independent session and a route guard, and the sign-in, sign-up, confirm, reset and sign-out screens are seeded against the component-kit@2 standard shell exports (SignInPage, Field, Button), so they work on every kit that provides it. It declares services.auth; the local issuer comes from api-go.

plugins.name: auth-hosted
plugins.description: The auth plugin for the hosted lane: sign-in on the app's Amazon Cognito hosted page by the authorization code flow with PKCE, no password field in the app. The API redirects, finishes the callback, verifies the ID token, keeps the session in HttpOnly cookies, and serves GET /api/me, sign-out, account deletion and an email domain rule; the web side adds a route guard and the sign-in, sign-out, account and refusal screens on component-kit@2. It declares services.auth.

plugins.name: auth-none
plugins.description: The auth plugin for an app with no sign-in: a stub identity seam for the Go API in which every request acts for one fixed owner, so a handler written against it works unchanged under a real sign-in. No screens, no middleware, no routes, and no requirements, so a web-only profile composes it too.

plugins.name: kit-carbon
plugins.description: The component-kit plugin for Svelte in the IBM Carbon style: the styled shell pieces (UI shell with side nav, forms, tables, dialogs, toasts, empty states) on carbon-components-svelte, in Carbon's white and Gray 100 themes, which pass WCAG 2.2 AA contrast. Carbon is not themeable by a visual-language plugin.

plugins.name: kit-gds
plugins.description: The component-kit plugin for Svelte in GOV.UK Design System style: the shell pieces (app shell with a text-only header and service navigation, button, form field, error summary, table, dialog) in GOV.UK Frontend v6 markup and classes, plus the GOV.UK design-system and accessibility skills (WCAG 2.2 AA, the public sector regulations, audit and statement material). No Crown and no GOV.UK logotype. Not themeable by a visual-language plugin.

plugins.name: look-business
plugins.description: Dense, exact and quiet: for enterprise and line-of-business web apps (admin, finance, operations) where staff live in tables all day. Navy neutrals, 2px corners, no elevation, compact rows and tabular figures.

plugins.name: look-startup
plugins.description: Crisp, quiet and fast: for SaaS and developer-tool products. One confident teal accent on near-neutral surfaces, generous whitespace, a strong type hierarchy with tight display tracking, hairlines and a soft layered shadow.

plugins.name: look-consumer
plugins.description: Friendly, warm and playful: for mobile-first personal and lifestyle web apps. Big thumb-sized targets, rounded type, 24px corners, a warm cream palette with a berry accent, a few things at a time.
